locator: §4.1, 'the status of an argument as valid depends, at least in part, on the words not shifting in meaning as we move from premise to premise'
interpretation: Geach's Frege point (Geach 1965, 449: a proposition may occur 'now asserted, now unasserted, and yet be recognizably the same proposition'), applied to validity: if content did not stay constant across embedded and unembedded occurrences, 'we would routinely commit a fallacy of equivocation'. Read as a necessary condition on the validity of a modus ponens: its minor premise must mean the same free-standing and in the antecedent. 'At least in part' is respected: constant meaning is not claimed to suffice. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
